content.text:
There is a common settings-change point, but it is the wrong place to force a save.

Both editor changes and Agent preset changes eventually pass through [`Tab::update_dirty()`](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp:1221) and [`Tab::on_presets_changed()`](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Tab.cpp:2108). Effective changes then reach [`Plater::on_config_change()`](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:16843).

Forcing a save there would:

- Run for individual field changes and sometimes individual keystrokes.
- Include preset selection, calibration setup, normalization, and automatic adjustments.
- Reintroduce the excessive writes and UI pauses we just removed.
- Perform the 3MF export synchronously on the UI thread through [`ProjectAutosave::save_now()`](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:893).

There is no single shared “editing has finished” event because human and Agent edits have different boundaries:

- Human editor: [`ParamsDialog` close handler](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/ParamsDialog.cpp:39).
- Agent edits: the Agent turn boundary already calls `save_now()`. ([ShellController.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:326))
- Project close/switch: the managed project release callback already calls `save_now()`. ([ShellController.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ShellController.cpp:329))
- Other settings changes: periodic autosave detects the complete effective configuration through `full_config_secure()` after a quiet period.

We could add one small human-editor boundary call so closing the settings window immediately checkpoints the project. That would improve save timing, but it would **not clear the reusable-preset dirty state**. Project saving and reusable preset saving are separate.

Automatically saving the reusable preset is not safe as a general solution:

- System presets are read only and require creating a named copy.
- User presets are shared across projects, so silently overwriting one would change future projects.
- Project embedded presets belong in the project checkpoint rather than the global preset library.

The actual source of the unwanted close dialog is simpler. In managed mode, [`Plater::close_with_confirm()`](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:14747) currently runs the legacy reusable-preset check **before** invoking the managed project save callback. The managed save already captures all effective settings.

My recommendation is:

1. At managed project release, save the project checkpoint.
2. Skip the legacy reusable-preset prompt in managed mode.
3. Optionally force an immediate checkpoint when the human settings editor closes, if the small close-time pause is acceptable.
4. Keep reusable preset saving explicit, because it changes settings outside the current project.

That is the smallest coherent fix. Hooking forced saves into the shared mutation path would bring back the write amplification problem. No code was changed during this review.

The checkpoint exports a 3MF using `full_config_secure()`. That configuration is built from the currently edited process, printer, and filament settings—not merely the original reusable preset values. ([PresetBundle.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/libslic3r/PresetBundle.cpp:3865), [ProjectAutosave.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectAutosave.cpp:393))

For example:

- Reusable preset says bed temperature `100`.
- The project changes it to `110`.
- A checkpoint completes.
- Restoring that checkpoint restores `110`.
- The reusable preset can remain `100`.

The only gap is timing: if the app crashes immediately after a change and before the next checkpoint finishes, that latest change may be absent. Forcing a checkpoint when the settings window closes would close that gap for settings changed there. Agent changes are already force-saved when the Agent finishes responding, and closing or replacing the current project also force-saves it.

The warning appears because this line runs before JusPrin saves the project:

[Plater.cpp](/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/src/slic3r/GUI/Plater.cpp:14750)

```cpp
if (second_check && !second_check(false)) return wxID_CANCEL;
```

That line was added by our autosave commit. It is not original Orca code. Removing it would make the sequence:

1. Save the current project and its edited settings.
2. Close or replace the project.
3. Do not show Orca’s reusable-preset warning.

This is already how creating a new project and opening another project behave. Application close is the inconsistent case.

This is the minimum-footprint solution:

- Delete one line from a block we already added.
- Add no new changed location in Orca code.
- Leave normal Orca behavior untouched when JusPrin’s automatic project saving is unavailable.
- Keep the close operation cancellable if the checkpoint fails.
- Avoid relying on a global “remember my choice” preference, which would also affect classic Orca workflows.

A solution entirely inside the JusPrin directory is not safely available because Orca displays the warning before calling the JusPrin save callback. Intercepting window-close events from JusPrin would duplicate Orca’s shutdown logic and be much riskier.

So I recommend removing that one line and adding a focused test proving that:

- edited settings are captured;
- the warning callback is not called;
- closing is canceled if the checkpoint fails.
